name: Arkansas
agency: Arkansas Department of Finance and Administration, Office of Driver Services (licenses); knowledge and skills tests given by Arkansas State Police
permitAge: 14 (learner's license, ages 14-15), after vision screening and written knowledge test

teen.holdPermit: 6 consecutive months with no moving violation convictions (secondary sources)
teen.nightLimit: Intermediate license: no driving 11 p.m. to 4 a.m. unless with parent/guardian, to or from work, school or church activity, or emergency (secondary sources; exceptions vary)
teen.passengerLimit: Intermediate license: one unrelated passenger under 21 (secondary sources)
teen.phone: Under 18: no phone use while driving, even hands-free, except emergencies (secondary law). 18-20: hands-free only. All drivers: no texting or social media; handheld calls banned in school zones and in work zones when workers are present.

notes: Graduated license: learner's 14-15 (with licensed driver 21+), intermediate 16-17, unrestricted at 18 with clean record for previous 12 months (DFA page, via search snippet).
Intermediate requires no serious violations or at-fault crashes in previous 6 months (DFA).
Early unrestricted license possible at 16-17 for high school diploma/GED, emancipation, marriage, military enlistment (DFA).
Exam: 25 questions, 20 correct (80%) reported only by third-party sites; not confirmed on an official page. Given at State Police testing sites per secondary sources.
Supervised driving hours: one secondary source says 50 (10 at night); not confirmed, left null.
Rural interstates: 75 mph cars, 70 mph trucks; urban interstates 65 (GHSA, ArDOT 2020).
Move over (Ark. Code 27-51-310): emergency, ArDOT, utility, tow vehicles with flashing lights; move to farthest lane or slow down; fine $250-$1,000 (ASP 2025).
School bus (Isaac's Law): stop at least 30 feet; opposite direction may proceed only on 4+ lane highway with median at least 20 feet wide; fine up to $2,500.
Right on red after full stop unless signed; left on red only one-way to one-way.
